title: Discord Chats are Coming to Google Search: How to Opt Out
text:
Discord conversations on large public servers will soon reach audiences far beyond their communities, raising privacy concerns.
Discord is making a policy change that will make conversations from its largest public servers discoverable in search engines, including Google, raising privacy concerns among users whose conversations were previously confined to the platform.
The change applies to Discoverable Servers — communities with at least 1,000 members listed in Discord’s public directory that do not require an invitation to join.
From Nov. 16, every Discoverable Server will have a web page that may include summaries of public channel discussions. From mid-December, individual messages posted in eligible channels may appear in web search, Discord said Tuesday. Messages posted before the rollout will not be included, while usernames and avatars will be excluded from published messages.
Example of an individual message being shown online. Source: Discord
Discord said the shift of online communities from message boards to its servers had made useful answers harder to find. “This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this,” the company said.
The move has drawn criticism from users concerned about their conversations reaching an audience outside of their intended community, even if the servers are public in the first place.
Related: Starknet introduces wallet privacy feature for DeFi activity
Others welcomed the change, saying it could make useful answers easier to find. One user in Discord’s announcement thread called it “very much necessary,” while another said moving communities from forums to Discord had made their discussions harder to find through search.
The change could also affect cryptocurrency communities that use Discord for technical discussions, support and project announcements.
Cointelegraph found nearly 800 servers tagged “cryptocurrency,” around 1,400 tagged “trading” and more than 700 tagged “finance” in Discord’s public directory. Discord said there are over 63,000 total discoverable servers on its platform.
Users have until the message-sharing rollout begins in mid-December to opt out before their posts become eligible to appear online. Discord said the feature will be disabled by default for users in Australia, the EU, the European Economic Area, the UK, Canada, Brazil and South Korea. Teen users will also be excluded.
To opt out, users should go into User Settings > Data & Privacy and switch off “Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages.” The setting covers every Discoverable Server a user belongs to, according to Discord’s guidance.
How users can opt out of having their messages visible on web pages. Source: Discord
Users can also disable the feature after launch, but it only protects messages sent after the opt-out. Users who want an eligible message removed must delete it from Discord, and Discord warns that search engines may retain cached copies for some time.
Server administrators can also prevent messages from individual channels or entire servers from appearing on public web pages and in search results through Server Settings > Web Presence.
They can separately disable discussion summaries, which are scheduled to begin rolling out in November.

title: Datavault AI stock plummets 50% after firm says it cannot withdraw bitcoin tied to $150 million deal
text: Datavault AI Inc. (DVLT) shares plunged nearly 50% on Tuesday after the company disclosed that it has been unable to withdraw a significant amount of bitcoin (BTC) from a third-party wallet maintained by Bitconomy exchange. DVLT closed near $0.067 on Tuesday, down 49.6% from the prior day's closing price of $0.133. Nearly 250 million shares changed hands on the day, an eightfold increase from the prior trading day. In a Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Oct. 26, the company said more than a year of financial statements cannot be relied upon because of an accounting error from a large equity transaction involving bitcoin. The issue centers on a September 2025 securities purchase agreement with Scilex Holding Co., under which Scilex agreed to buy 15 million shares of Datavault AI common stock and a pre-funded warrant covering more than 263.9 million shares for $150 million, payable in bitcoin — approximately 1,328.43 BTC at a rate of $112,915.52 per bitcoin. Bitcoin was credited to a company digital wallet at Biconomy Pte. Ltd. through an offchain transfer. Between September 2025 and January 2026, Datavault AI sold a portion of the credited Bitcoin back to Scilex for about $40.5 million in cash. In June 2026, the company requested to withdraw bitcoin from the Biconomy wallet to an external account. As of Oct. 26, Datavault said it has been unable to complete the withdrawal. The filing provided no further explanation on why it was unable to do so. The Block has reached out to Datavault AI and Scilex for comment. Uncertainty Datavault AI determined that the bitcoin associated with the Scilex transaction did not meet the requirements for recognition as a company digital asset, noting that the amounts should instead have been recorded as a subscription receivable from the equity issuance, presented as a reduction of stockholders’ equity. Management is reassessing its going-concern evaluation because it previously recognized bitcoin balances as a source of liquidity, and collection of amounts from Scilex remains uncertain. The company said it intends to restate the affected financial statements but has not yet determined the timing of those filings. It added that the restatements are expected to reduce its total assets by $8.1 million, $92.2 million, $57.1 million, and $49 million as of Sept. 30, 2025, Dec. 31, 2025, March 31, 2026, and June 30, 2026, respectively.

title: Bithumb Investigates Extent of Data Leak After Internal Hack
text:
The breach impacted its in-house mobile system, used by employees for work and information sharing.
South Korea’s crypto exchange Bithumb is investigating the extent of a data leak caused by a hack of its internal mobile system earlier this week, Yonhap News Agency reported Wednesday.
Bithumb discovered the breach of its in-house mobile system — the platform used by employees to communicate internally — on Tuesday and notified the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission that day, according to Yonhap, which cited industry sources.
The exchange is investigating the scope of the attack, including whether member data was leaked.
“We are analyzing the exact scope, including the possibility of member information being involved,” Bithumb told Yonhap. “We will provide an official announcement this morning. However, the internal work system is separated from the virtual asset trading system, so customer virtual assets cannot be accessed through this breach.”
Cointelegraph reached out to Bithumb for further comment.
The incident adds to a recent wave of cyberattacks in Korea’s financial sector.
During a meeting at the Financial Supervisory Authority headquarters on Wednesday, Governor Lee Chan-jin said cyberattacks had hit 16 South Korean financial firms as of Oct. 14.
The Korea Times reports that asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities were also recent victims of cyberattacks.
Daishin Securities said that personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers had been leaked. Mirae Asset Global Investments said it had blocked abnormal external access to some web systems and was investigating the incident. The company said investor information was not affected, according to Yonhap.

title: Coinbase says user funds are safe after vendor exposes customer data
text:
Nasdaq-listed cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has denied reports of a hack, saying customer funds are safe.
The exchange clarified that the incident that led to the breach of customer data originated at Amplitude, a third-party analytics provider, and not the exchange itself. The exposed data includes only a “small subset” of contact information, alongside data related to other Amplitude clients, Coinbase Support’s X handle said.
It said the exchange is informing impacted customers via email as required by law, while stressing that the exchange’s systems have not seen any unauthorized access.
The disclosure puts the focus on supply-chain risk, meaning customers can face security risks via third parties even when a company’s core infrastructure remains secure. Coinbase did not specify how many customers were affected or exactly which contact-data fields were involved, leaving key details unresolved.
While customer funds remain safe, exposed email addresses and phone numbers can still serve as valuable raw material for phishing and social-engineering attacks, even if passwords, private keys, and funds were not compromised.
CoinDesk reached out to Coinbase for comment on the matter.

title: Robinhood CEO says Tokenized Equities in US Needs Lasting Rules
text:
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says tokenized equities need more than a temporary SEC exemption to flourish in the US.
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev says uncertainty over the longevity of US tokenization rules could prevent investors from committing substantial assets to tokenized markets, despite the securities regulator opening a temporary path for onchain stock trading this year.
Speaking during Robinhood’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Tenev welcomed the SEC’s innovation exemption but said further rulemaking or legislation would be needed to provide longer-term regulatory certainty.
“As far as the innovation exemption goes, I think it’s a really positive step... I do think more needs to be done to give people a little bit of certainty because as we talk to customers, I think the uncertainty of what happens in five years is likely to be an impediment to, like, putting serious assets onto this technology.”
Tokenized stock offerings have faced resistance from traditional issuers. Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs were among 16 companies that objected to their shares being offered on the proposed OKXICE venue, while AMC CEO Adam Aron separately criticized Robinhood’s tokenized stock products.
Despite the regulatory uncertainty, Binance Research projects that the tokenized equities market could grow to $349 billion by 2030 under its base-case scenario, from $4.43 billion as of Sept. 15.
Related: SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinations
“So I still think some rule-making or legislation is going to be necessary, even though, of course, it’s a positive step, and we hope to have more to share on our own US tokenization plans in the near future,” said Tenev.
Asked about private-company stock tokens, Tenev said Robinhood intends to launch those products overseas, subject to regulatory arrangements. In the US, Tenev said the company is working to find a path that satisfies current accreditation constraints.
Robinhood offers around 200 stock tokens on Robinhood Chain. The products are backed by underlying shares but structured as tokenized debt securities, providing economic exposure without the same shareholder rights as conventional stocks.
That distinction leaves their current structure outside the SEC’s innovation exemption, which requires equivalent rights, including dividends and voting rights.
Tenev’s comments came as Robinhood reported a 55% year-on-year fall in cryptocurrency revenue to $120 million in the third quarter, while crypto notional trading volume declined 38% to $50 billion.
Trading volume on the Robinhood app fell 48% to $21 billion, while Bitstamp volume fell 28% to $29 billion.
Robinhood’s prediction market business went in the opposite direction. Event-contract revenue rose sixfold to $173 million, while contracts traded increased more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion.
Across the wider business, total net revenue rose 12% to a record $1.42 billion, below analyst expectations. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.60, missing estimates by 4 cents.

title: BTC, ETH price news: Bitcoin nears $81,000 ahead of Fed decision as ZEC jumps 8%
text:
Bitcoin climbed nearly 2% to just under $81,000 as of Wednesday Asian morning hours, clawing back the weekend’s slip to nearly $79,000 as traders braced for the Federal Reserve’s rate decision later in the day.
ZEC led the majors, jumping 8% to about $1,320 and putting it back above $1,300 after Monday’s selloff. HYPE added nearly 5% to about $81. XRP and DOGE rose roughly 3%, while ether gained 2% to just above $2,350 and SOL climbed about 2% to $102. BNB rose 1%, and TRX lagged with a gain of less than 1%, according to CoinDesk data.
The bounce came a day after Galaxy told investors that now is the time to accumulate bitcoin.
“We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance,” Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, said in the note.
Thorn said the bottom likely came in June, when bitcoin traded under $58,000. He pointed to bitcoin’s move back above its 50-week moving average — the average of its last 50 weekly closes, which traders use to judge the longer-term trend — along with lighter selling pressure and rising U.S. debt. That’s a confident call for a market that has struggled to hold $80,000.
Traders will now be listening to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for any hint of a December rate hike. A hike would make borrowing more expensive and tends to pull money out of riskier assets like crypto.

title: Bithumb hacked through employee system as South Korean financial firms face cyberattacks
text:
Bithumb, South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, said earlier Wednesday an outsider broke into the internal mobile system its employees use to work and message each other and that personal information was taken.
No crypto funds were reported lost as of Asian afternoon hours. Bithumb is the second-largest exchange in South Korea by trading volumes.
The exchange found the intrusion on Tuesday and reported to the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission, according to Korean media. It told Yonhap it was analyzing the exact scope, “including the possibility of member information being involved.”
It said the breached system runs separately from its trading platform, so “customer virtual assets cannot be accessed through this breach.” It has not said whether deposits or withdrawals were affected or how many people’s data was exposed.
Bithumb was one of three financial firms the Financial Supervisory Service said it was assessing on Wednesday. Daishin Securities said personal and credit information for 38,490 of its customers leaked in an outside attack. Mirae Asset Global Investments said it blocked abnormal access to some of its web systems and that investor information was not affected.
“I understand that major financial investment companies experienced overall hacking incidents yesterday,” FSS Governor Lee Chan-jin told a meeting with bank holding company chairs. Earlier in the month he said cyberattacks had hit 16 South Korean financial firms as of Oct. 14.
Meanwhile, this is a second hit to Bithumb’s controls this year.
In February it mistakenly credited customers with 620,000 BTC, worth more than $40 billion at the time, instead of 620,000 won. CEO Lee Jae-won blamed the error on weak internal controls at the time, saying the exchange was “acutely aware of the deficiency in internal system control.”

title: Bitcoin treasury stock plunges 50% after firm says it can’t access its BTC
text:
Datavault AI (DVLT) shares plunged nearly 50% on Tuesday after a filing revealed that the company had been unable to withdraw bitcoin from crypto exchange Biconomy since June and would have to restate its financial results.
The stock closed at $0.067, down 49.55%, with roughly 244 million shares traded.
The problem traces back to a September 2025 agreement with Scilex Holding Company, which agreed to purchase $150 million of Datavault shares and warrants using bitcoin.
Scilex credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault’s account at Biconomy through off-chain transfers, meaning the balances changed within the exchange rather than through transactions on Bitcoin’s blockchain. Datavault subsequently sold 491.4 BTC back to Scilex for about $40.5 million in cash.
But the transfer could not be completed when it requested a withdrawal to an external account in June, the comapny said, and remained incomplete as of Monday’s filing.
Biconomy was also involved in supplying the bitcoin behind the investment. Scilex’s June financial report says it sold $200 million of shares in its subsidiary Semnur to Biconomy for bitcoin, then used $150 million to buy Datavault securities.
Datavault now says the bitcoin credited through Scilex’s investment should have been recorded as an amount Scilex owed for the shares. That amount would reduce shareholders’ equity instead of appearing among Datavault’s cryptocurrency assets.
The correction is expected to reduce reported assets by $92.2 million at the end of 2025 and $49 million as of June 2026. Datavault had counted those bitcoin balances as money it could draw on to keep the business running, but must now revisit the assessment.
CoinDesk contacted Biconomy about the withdrawal request and the bitcoin backing Datavault’s account and did not receive a response as of Asian afternoon hours Wednesday.

title: Coinbase Denies Breach, Says Vendor Exposed Customer Data
text:
Coinbase said that an incident at analytics vendor Amplitude exposed some customers’ contact data, but it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its own systems.
Some Coinbase customers’ contact information was exposed in a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude, the exchange said Wednesday.
The incident impacted a “small subset” of Coinbase customers, along with other Amplitude clients, Coinbase Support said on X.
Coinbase denied that its own systems had been breached and said customer funds were not affected.
The disclosure adds to Wednesday’s reports of cyberattacks affecting both crypto exchanges and traditional financial firms. In South Korea, Bithumb is investigating whether a breach of its internal work platform exposed customer information, while brokerage Daishin Securities reported a leak of personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers.
Cointelegraph contacted Coinbase to find out how many customers were affected but had not received a response by publication.
In May 2025, Coinbase disclosed a separate data breach that impacted less than 1% of its monthly transacting users. The exchange estimated reimbursement and remediation costs at up to $400 million.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Gain $286M as Ether ETF Outflows Deepen
text:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $286 million over two days, narrowing October’s net outflows to $26 million as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index remained neutral.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted about $176 million in net inflows on Tuesday, extending their recovery to a second consecutive trading day.
The inflows rose from $110 million on Monday, bringing the two-day total to $286 million, according to SoSoValue data.
The rebound followed nearly $774 million in withdrawals on Thursday and Friday. October net outflows narrowed to about $26 million through Tuesday, while year-to-date net inflows stood at roughly $850 million.
Market sentiment also edged higher. Alternative.me’s Crypto Fear & Greed Index rose to 51 from 48 the previous day, remaining in “Neutral” territory. The reading was still below 63, or “Greed,” a week earlier.
Bitcoin (BTC) traded at about $80,818 at the time of publication, up 1.6% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.
Meanwhile, US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs continued to see withdrawals, recording about $149 million in net outflows on Monday and Tuesday after four straight weeks of net outflows.
Their October net outflows reached $1.32 billion through Tuesday, putting the month on track for the largest net withdrawals since November 2025.

title: Securitize (SECZ) adds Stellar blockchain as institutional tokenization gathers steam
text:
Securitize (SECZ), which converts real-world assets such as equity and debt into tokens that can be traded like cryptocurrencies, said it added Stellar to its list of supported blockchains.
The company already works closely with Ethereum, Solana and Avalanche and is known for issuing and managing BlackRock’s BUIDL tokenized money-market fund.
Tokenization, the process of bringing assets onto a blockchain, has been generating headlines in recent months, with a growing number of companies saying they’re offering, or planning to offer, versions of shares, bonds and commodities that can be traded around the clock with few, if any, geographic restrictions.
Stellar is known for being a fast and scalable blockchain, where decentralized assets can be configured for customer identification (KYC), clawbacks and sanctions compliance, the firms said at Meridian 2026, the Stellar Development Foundation’s annual conference in Lisbon. Franklin Templeton runs a tokenized money market fund on Stellar, and MoneyGram moves money across it daily.
“The Stellar network has built the fourth-largest ecosystem for tokenized real-world assets, which speaks to the strength of its network and the growing institutional demand for tokenization,” said Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo in a statement.
Stellar, founded in 2017, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in July, putting its own stock on Solana (SOL) and Avalanche (AVAX) at the same time. The shares, which rose as high as $13.70 on the first day of trading, closed at $xx.xx on Tuesday.

title: Moody's assigns investment-grade ratings to Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin
text: Moody’s Ratings assigned Ripple's U.S. dollar-denominated stablecoin A2 long-term and P-1 short-term deposit ratings, both investment-grade marks. The agency said the A2 long-term deposit rating reflects its assessment of the credit quality and market value of RLUSD's reserve assets, reserve coverage, liquidity and redemption arrangements. It also pointed to the segregation of the reserve and its custody with third parties, as well as operational, technological, legal, regulatory and other structural considerations. The P-1 rating aligns with the long-term rating, Moody's said. "The Reserve is predominantly invested in highly liquid, short-duration U.S. government assets and cash," Moody's said. "[Standard Custody & Trust Company] targets 103% Reserve coverage, which exceeds the minimum coverage level associated with the rating." The majority of RLUSD's reserve assets comprises U.S. Treasury bills, other short-term U.S. government assets, and cash, held with The Bank of New York Mellon (BNY), which is an Aa1-rated custodian, according to Moody's. The agency further noted that the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027, will strengthen protections for reserve assets and stablecoin holders, including shielding required reserves from an issuer's bankruptcy estate. Total fiat-backed stablecoin supply | The Block The ratings were assigned under Moody's Stablecoin methodology published in March 2026. Deterioration in the credit quality or market value of reserve assets, a decline in coverage, or weaker liquidity or redemption capacity could lead to lower ratings. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said RLUSD is the first stablecoin to receive an investment-grade rating from Moody's, calling it a "massive validation" for the project. Earlier this week, Ripple received final approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank. The national charter, as a federally regulated platform, is authorized to manage the segregated reserves supporting RLUSD, act as collateral trustee of those reserves for RLUSD holders, and provide fiduciary digital asset custody services. The U.S. dollar stablecoin, launched in December 2024, has grown to a $2.5 billion market capitalization. Ripple said it's mainly used as an instrument within Ripple's payment infrastructure and as collateral in Ripple Prime.

title: Bitcoin has soared over 50% on average after prior mid terms.
text:
Both crypto and Wall Street could be in for a strong run after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, if history is a guide.
Since its inception in 2009, bitcoin BTC$84.459,46, the largest cryptocurrency by market value, has seen four midterms. Leaving out 2010, when the market was tiny and fringe, the other three saw prices for the cryptocurrency rise an average of 53.7% in the 12 months after Election Day, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk. The returns here refer to the percentage rise from the daily close (00:00 UTC) on Election Day to the close on the same date a year later.
Bitcoin surged 1,579% in the 12 months after the 2010 midterm, but the market was fringe and too small then for that figure to be reliable.
If history repeats, bitcoin’s recent subdued price action around $80,000 could pave the way for another leg higher after Nov. 3. BTC has already bounced more than 35% since bottoming out below $60,000 in June. Some analysts believe now is the time to buy and hold crypto, as a new bull run is upon us.
Still, history is too limited to draw firm conclusions, and the post-midterm surges in BTC seen over the years may have more to do with the four-year cycle than U.S. politics.
Bitcoin tends to move in cycles of roughly four years, built around the mining reward halving, an inbuilt code in the Bitcoin blockchain that reduces the per block BTC produced and given to miners by 50% every four years.
After each of the four halvings to date, BTC rallied sharply, peaked 12 to 18 months later and then sliding into a bear market. Those bear markets played out in midterm years – 2014, 2018, 2022 and now 2026. So the rebound that followed the midterms may have been a fresh cycle start rather than politics at work.
The S&P 500 has a much longer record, and it also points up, a positive sign for bitcoin and other risk assets.
Since 1950, the index has averaged a 15.17% gain in the year after midterms, against 7.30% in all other years, according to Hartford Funds.
The 2026 elections could change how President Donald Trump operates in his final two years in the White House.
If Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress, the politics over the record federal debt may heat up, as the debt limit issue is still unresolved and talks over the same may complicate. Trump’s push for $350 billion in mandatory defense funding may not stand a chance, according to Brookings. Democrats could use legislative hurdles to arrest funding for Middle East escalations.
Speaking of crypto, Democratic committee chairs could investigate conflicts of interest tied to Trump’s personal crypto profits. Democratic lawmakers have already sent oversight letters on the president’s crypto ties and family business ventures. Trump’s memecoin, launched in January 2025, has also led to heavy losses for retail investors.
That said, the Supreme Court’s ruling in Trump v. Slaughter left most financial regulators under White House control, so Congress could do little to stop the administration from promoting crypto.
For now, markets have largely priced in a divided federal government, with Democrats expected to retake at least one chamber of Congress.

title: Brazil’s largest lender becomes first bank to formalize crypto brokerage under new rules
text:
Itaú Unibanco, Brazil’s largest private bank, formalized its cryptocurrency trading and custody operations under the country’s new digital-asset rules, becoming the first bank in the country to do so.
The lender submitted its notification to the central bank on Tuesday, ahead of an Oct. 30 compliance deadline, according to local news outlet Valor Econômico
The regulatory framework allows banks already authorized by the central bank to follow a notification process for offering crypto services. Dedicated virtual-asset service providers (VASPs), in contrast, must apply for operating authorization.
Itaú Unibanco offers 15 cryptoassets, including bitcoin BTC$84,459.46, ether ETH$2,490.55 and the dollar-pegged stablecoin USDC, according to its website. It has not disclosed customer numbers or trading volumes for the service, which started in December 2023.
Itaú’s combination of trading and custody corresponds to the brokerage category under the rules.
The central bank’s Resolution 520 took effect on Feb. 2 and gave eligible financial institutions already active in crypto 270 days to notify the regulator. Submissions must include an independent technical certification showing they meet its requirements. Those that miss the deadline must stop providing crypto services within 30 days.
The same deadline applies to authorization applications from dedicated crypto providers already operating when the rules took effect. Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin has said it is seeking authorization to operate as a virtual-asset brokerage.
In September, the central bank pushed to Nov. 6 the date from which banks and other authorized institutions are barred from doing crypto business with unauthorized providers.

"Coinbase has not had a data breach," the company's support account said in a tweet on Tuesday night. "Amplitude, an analytics vendor, experienced a security incident which impacted a small subset of Coinbase customer contact data, among other Amplitude customers."
Coinbase has not had a data breach.
Amplitude, an analytics vendor, experienced a security incident which impacted a small subset of Coinbase customer contact data, among other Amplitude customers.
We’ve found no evidence of unauthorized access to Coinbase systems, and…
— Coinbase Support (@CoinbaseSupport) October 28, 2026
Coinbase said it had found no evidence of unauthorized access to its systems and that customer funds were “not impacted.” It is notifying affected customers and regulators in line with its legal obligations.
The company did not say how many customers were affected, what kinds of contact data were exposed, or when the incident took place. Nor did it name the other Amplitude customers affected.
Coinbase disclosed a far more serious incident in May 2025, when it said cybercriminals had bribed overseas customer support agents to steal personal data belonging to less than 1% of its monthly transacting users. The exchange refused a $20 million ransom demand and instead offered a $20 million bounty for information leading to the attackers' arrest.
A later filing with the Maine attorney general put the number of affected customers at 69,461, with data including names, addresses, masked Social Security numbers and government ID images exposed.
Crypto firms have repeatedly seen customer data exposed through partners. In September, hardware wallet maker Trezor said a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk had exposed the names, phone numbers and home addresses of 67,000 U.S. customers, on top of nearly 14,000 it had disclosed in August. Some of the records dated back to 2019, years after ShipMonk had told Trezor they were deleted. Trezor warned affected customers to watch for fake emails, calls and letters, and about risks to their physical security.
At the time, cybercrime consultant David Sehyeon Baek told Decrypt that a letter carrying a name and home address signals "we can locate you," and that stolen data stays useful for years because people rarely move or change their numbers.

title: Nearly 90% of large businesses are embracing tokenized cash to speed up payments: DBS
text:
Large businesses are using or testing tokenized money to improve cash management and cross-border payments, with 88% of respondents to a DBS survey reporting live deployments or pilots, the Singapore bank said.
The report found 24% had deployed the technology at scale, while 43% had limited live use in selected markets. Another 21% were running pilots or proofs of concept, leaving 12% exploring the technology or not using it.
DBS commissioned EY to conduct the study, which polled 422 business and finance leaders across 11 markets, including the U.S., China, Germany and the U.K. All represented organizations with annual revenue above $500 million.
Stablecoins led the instruments respondents were using or planning to adopt, at 63%, followed by tokenized deposits at 53% and tokenized money market funds at 52% according to the study.
Faster payments were among the expected benefits. Some 71% of respondents said they already experienced improvements in real-time cross-border payments or expected them within two years, while 65% reported the same for treasury liquidity management.
Regulatory uncertainty, security risks and integration difficulties remained obstacles, with nearly two-thirds wanting banks to provide a single point of access to the tokenized money ecosystem, while 63% sought help with pilots and integration.
“For companies, fragmentation may add complexities and compliance obligations,” Lim Soon Chong, DBS’s group head of global transaction services, said. “The future will be defined by new forms of money and technology, and also shaped by trusted anchors who can orchestrate value movement across multiple networks.”
DBS itself offers the infrastructure the survey examines. It launched DBS Token Services in 2024, connecting its permissioned blockchain with its payment systems to support round-the-clock settlement and payments governed by preset conditions.
Other banks have reported live corporate use. Citi said at its May investor day that hundreds of clients were moving close to $1 billion daily through Citi Token Services, primarily to manage liquidity and working capital.
In September, DBS and Citi completed a weekend dollar payment between Singapore and New York using tokenized deposits through the Swift Digital Ledger. DBS said the transaction settled in minutes, allowing funds to move outside traditional banking hours.

title: Bithumb Says Hackers Accessed Internal System, Leaking Personal Data - Decrypt
text:
Bithumb, South Korea's second-largest crypto exchange, said an unauthorized outside party had accessed its internal mobile groupware system, resulting in a leak of personal information, according to Yonhap News Agency.
The exchange is investigating whether customer data was compromised, Reuters reported, citing Yonhap. An industry source told Yonhap that some personal information belonging to Bithumb customers had been leaked.
Bithumb was one of three South Korean financial firms to report data breaches on Wednesday, local time. Brokerage Daishin Securities said the personal information of 38,490 customers, including names, email addresses and mobile phone numbers, was leaked after it detected signs of unauthorized access last week. It said it would compensate customers for any resulting damage in accordance with the law.
Asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments also confirmed a hacking incident, and financial authorities have begun an inspection.
Spokespeople for the three firms could not be immediately reached for comment by Reuters. The breaches follow a wave of hacking attacks on 16 South Korean financial firms, including banks, that had caused around 100,000 data leaks, the Financial Services Commission said earlier this month, according to Reuters.
The Korean breaches were reported the same day Coinbase said a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude had exposed some of its customers' contact data. Binance founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao listed all four incidents in a tweet on Wednesday, warning that leaked exchange data "is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering."
1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.
In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 3. Mirae Asset4. Daishin Securities
— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 28, 2026
"You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself," Zhao wrote, urging users to sign up to each exchange with a unique email alias, avoid text message-based two-factor authentication and ask their phone carrier for a number lock. Leaked addresses and holdings data "have led to real-world extortion and robberies," he added.
Separately, South Korea's Science Ministry and the Korea Internet & Security Agency have urged website operators to check for recently disclosed flaws in PHP, the programming language behind much of the web, which let attackers run commands on a server without logging in. Bithumb has not said how its system was accessed.
The breach is the latest setback for Bithumb in 2026. In February, the exchange mistakenly credited 695 users with a total of 620,000 BTC, worth about $43 billion at the time, during a promotion meant to hand out small cash rewards. The deposits existed only on Bithumb's internal ledger, and the exchange said it recovered 99.7% of the Bitcoin.
In March, South Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit fined Bithumb 36.8 billion won ($24.6 million) and ordered a six-month partial suspension over anti-money laundering failures, but a Seoul court blocked the suspension in April.
Bithumb has since set out a three-stage plan to list on the stock market in 2028, while its CEO, Lee Jae-won, was booked as a bribery suspect in June over the alleged hiring of a National Assembly member's son.

title: Google to preview a new crypto security system as private-key hacks mount
text:
Google to showcase a new security system designed to help banks and other financial institutions safeguard and move cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets at its inaugural digital assets symposium in New York City on Wednesday.
The product, officially named Google Multi-Party Compute (MPC), is in private preview and is not yet generally available. Several design partners and major financial institutions are testing the technology, Google told CoinDesk. Alphabet, the parent company, has also begun using it to secure its own digital assets on the Ethereum and Solana blockchains.
Google did not identify the institutions testing the service or specify which digital assets Alphabet is securing. The company plans to make Google Multi-Party Compute commercially available in early 2027, but has not disclosed pricing.
MPC isn't new to digital assets, nor is Google's involvement in the technology. The idea is to split a private key into individual fragments and distribute them across multiple separate systems, so there is no single point of failure. In 2023, Google published guidance explaining how customers could build MPC-based digital-asset systems using its Confidential Space infrastructure.
Google said it has not previously offered a dedicated MPC custody product for cryptocurrencies. Its existing production services include Google Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) and Cloud HSM, which institutions use to manage and protect cryptographic keys. The new offering brings MPC-based signing, transaction policies and key recovery into a purpose-built service for digital assets, rather than requiring customers to assemble those capabilities themselves.
The move comes as banks and other financial companies explore using blockchains to issue tokenized assets, process payments and offer digital asset custody services. Those activities require institutions to securely authorize transactions that, once completed on a blockchain, generally cannot be reversed.
“Digital asset adoption and tokenization are at an inflection point. As regulated financial institutions begin adopting blockchains and tokenization, they need scalable, proven infrastructure to secure their clients’ assets," Rich Widmann, director of digital assets strategy at Google Cloud, told CoinDesk.
An attacker who gains control of the private key protecting a wallet may be able to transfer its assets without the owner's permission, making key management a critical security challenge for institutions entering the market.
The threat has already cost the crypto industry billions of dollars over the years. According to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, compromised private keys accounted for 43.8% of cryptocurrency stolen in 2024. Separately, DeFiLlama data showed that as of June of this year, blockchain projects have lost a cumulative $16.69 billion to hacks and exploits, with roughly 40% of those losses attributed to private-key compromises.
Recent examples include stablecoin protocol Resolv, which suffered a March attack involving a compromised private key controlling a privileged account and weaknesses in its minting system, allowing a hacker to extract about $25 million. In June, attackers compromised the private keys of a Humanity Protocol foundation member and drained more than $32 million from at least 17 wallets. The breach also sent the project's token plunging more than 80%, showing how stolen credentials can cause losses beyond the assets directly taken.
The tech giant's new system aims to reduce the risk of relying on a single private key by using "multi-party computation," or MPC, which distributes control of a private key among multiple parties or computers. This way, instead of relying on a single key, the system requires several distinct pieces of cryptographic information to work together to authorize a transaction.
The complete private key is never stored in one place, according to Google, reducing the risk of an attacker taking control of the assets, even if a single machine is compromised. It also said that customers retain control of their key material and that the company cannot access it in unencrypted form, even when key shares are held on Google's infrastructure.
Google is also positioning the service as a response to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including threats involving artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing.
AI is already helping some cryptocurrency scammers operate on a larger scale, while researchers warn of potential future threats to the cryptography that protects digital assets.
Chainalysis found that cryptocurrency scams linked to AI-tool vendors extracted an average of $3.2 million per operation in 2025, compared with $719,000 for scams without such links — roughly 4.5 times as much. The findings suggest that AI may be helping fraudsters operate at a greater scale, although the report doesn't establish that AI directly caused the higher proceeds.
Recently, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that advances in AI could eventually uncover mathematical shortcuts that could break the digital signatures protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. Drake said such a breakthrough could emerge in a worst-case scenario within months rather than years, potentially before sufficiently powerful quantum computers arrive.
No AI system has demonstrated the ability to break the cryptographic signatures that protect Bitcoin or Ethereum wallets. AI systems can be used to uncover flaws in poorly encrypted tools, such as last week's certification authority debacle. Google's current MPC protections address threats such as compromised credentials and unauthorized transactions, rather than a hypothetical breakthrough against the underlying cryptography.
The system can help address existing threats by checking transactions against institutional rules before they are signed, potentially preventing transfers that violate preset limits or approval requirements. Those controls may reduce the risk of unauthorized transactions. However, the risk of legitimate users being deceived into authorizing malicious transactions may still pose a threat.
Quantum computing, although not imminent, poses a distinct, longer-term threat to institutions exploring digital asset adoption.
Google researchers have previously estimated that a sufficiently powerful future quantum computer could theoretically derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in roughly 9 minutes, assuming advanced preparation. While no quantum computer is currently capable of such an attack, about 6.9 million bitcoin have been reported as potentially vulnerable to future quantum attacks because their public keys have been exposed.
Google said its architecture is designed to support future upgrades to post-quantum cryptography, which seeks to protect digital signatures against attacks by sufficiently powerful quantum computers. The company said its MPC offering is designed to support conventional ECDSA and Ed25519 cryptographic signing algorithms at general availability.
Google did not provide a timetable for adding post-quantum signing capabilities but said the upgrades could be introduced as blockchain networks adopt the necessary cryptography, without requiring institutions to redesign their systems or interrupt operations.
A bank, for example, could keep one share of a cryptographic signing key in Google Cloud, another on its own hardware and a third with another cloud provider.
When the bank wants to move assets, the transaction enters Google's Confidential Space, where a policy engine checks it against the institution's rules before signing can begin, according to Google.
Those rules could include limits on the amount being transferred, restrictions on destination wallets and requirements for approval from several departments. The checks run inside Google's Confidential Space technology, which uses hardware-isolated computing environments designed to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.
Google says the system can also accommodate different cryptographic signing thresholds, such as requiring two of three or five of seven participants to jointly produce a transaction signature.
That flexibility is intended to address a concern for banks: they may want the convenience of cloud infrastructure without giving a single technology provider complete control over the credentials needed to move their assets.
Google said institutions can distribute those credentials across their own hardware, Google Cloud and competing cloud services. The company also said its system supports fast transaction signing and key recovery, although it did not provide independently verified performance comparisons with existing custody products.
Google's planned entry to the market brings one of the world's largest cloud providers closer to competing in a market already served by specialist crypto security firms, including Fireblocks, Fordefi and BitGo, which offer technology to help institutions protect and authorize blockchain transactions.
Google argues that its banking relationships and security expertise give it an edge over specialized crypto custody providers. It also sees an opportunity among banks wary of relying on providers that compete for the same customers, positioning itself as a neutral infrastructure supplier that lets institutions run their own custody businesses.
It's worth noting that Google's entry does not eliminate the need for institutions to assess the risks of their technology providers. Even when signing credentials are distributed across different environments, banks may still depend on Google for parts of the software, transaction policies and operational infrastructure.
The system's security also depends on how institutions configure it, protect their signing participants and control who can change transaction-approval rules.
The test will be whether institutions eventually see Google's offering as a safer alternative to specialized crypto custody providers and how much critical financial infrastructure they are willing to entrust to Google.

title: Mirae Asset Securities issues tokenized notes on Solana
text:
The company’s Hong Kong unit issued six-month notes under its $3 billion program, extending blockchain-based distribution to institutional investors.
The Hong Kong arm of Mirae Asset Securities, one of South Korea’s largest securities firms, has issued tokenized notes on Solana to institutional investors.
The transaction involved six-month floating-rate notes issued under the firm’s $3 billion structured note program, according to Wednesday’s announcement. Singapore-based digital market infrastructure operator Marketnode acted as an authorized distributor.
Mirae Asset Securities managed token issuance, payments and the notes’ lifecycle using its internal digital infrastructure. The company said the transaction could provide a model for distributing a wider range of structured products through blockchain-based channels.
The securities firm is part of South Korea’s Mirae Asset Financial Group, whose businesses span brokerage, investment banking, asset management and insurance.
The group has been expanding into digital assets, with affiliate Mirae Asset Consulting acquiring a controlling stake in crypto exchange Korbit in July, which has since rebranded to Digital X.
The group’s asset management arm, Mirae Asset Global Investments, operates the Global X and TIGER exchange-traded fund brands. Its website lists $275 billion in ETF assets under management as of June 2026 and describes its ETF business as the world’s 12th-largest.

title: Settlement Concerns Prompt Euronext to Suspend CoinShares’ Zcash ETP on Debut
text:
A Euronext spokesperson told Cointelegraph the suspension was due to “operational settlement requirements” and remains in effect until settlement operations are supported by the CSD.
Stock exchange operator Euronext suspended CoinShares’ Zcash exchange-traded product (ETP) on Wednesday, when it was scheduled to debut for trading on Euronext Paris.
In a Wednesday notice, the exchange operator said the CoinShares Zcash ETP (ZCSH) was suspended from trading on Euronext Paris until further notice. The notice did not provide a reason for the decision.
CoinShares’ Zcash ETP will remain suspended until “standard settlement operations can be fully supported by the Central Securities Depository (CSD),” Euronext’s press and communications manager, Flavio Bornancin-Tomasella, told Cointelegraph, adding that the measure was strictly limited to “operational settlement requirements.”
The suspension notice delays what would have been the fourth Zcash-based ETP listed in Europe. Other companies that launched Zcash ETPs earlier this year include 21Shares, Virtune and Valor.
CoinShares announced the planned launch of its ZCASH ETP on Euronext Paris earlier on Wednesday. Cointelegraph contacted CoinShares for comment on the matter but did not receive a response by publication.

title: XRP Ledger developers propose creating wallets with zero XRP for stablecoin payments
text:
Developers working on the XRP Ledger are testing a way to create blockchain accounts with zero XRP in them, potentially allowing payment applications and automated software to operate without first depositing the cryptocurrency into every wallet.
A code proposal submitted Oct. 15 introduces a transaction called SponsoredAccountCreate, which would allow an existing account to create another account and cover its reserve requirement.
XRP Ledger currently requires a minimum reserve of 1 XRP for each account. That money remains locked while the account is active, preventing the network from being flooded with empty wallets.
A company creating 100,000 separate accounts would need to set aside 100,000 XRP just to meet those reserve requirements.
Under the proposed system, a sponsoring account would cover the reserve, allowing the new wallet to keep a zero XRP balance. The network’s overall reserve obligation would remain, with the sponsor carrying the cost instead of the customer.
Sponsors could also cover transaction fees through a broader sponsorship mechanism, allowing applications to pay those charges on behalf of their users.
Ripple recently partnered with Stripe-owned Privy to bring embedded wallets to XRP Ledger applications. The integration is intended to support payments using XRP and Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, including automated payments made by AI agents.
Those wallets currently need XRP funding before they can become active, even when they’re only meant to hold stablecoins.
The proposed account-creation transaction builds on the broader Sponsored Fees and Reserves standard, which allows another account to pay network costs without taking control of the user’s private keys. The new code would create an account directly without sending it any XRP.
The pull request remains open, with two unresolved automated code-review findings. It also depends on sponsorship changes that have yet to activate on mainnet.
Those changes still need validator approval. The sponsorship amendment had 11 of the 35 votes it needs from the network’s trusted validators as of Oct. 19, according to XRPL Dashboard, well short of the 29 required.

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
Robinhood missed on both revenue and EPS on Tuesday, despite crypto beating expectations. But the more interesting things happened on the call.
Revenue came in at a record $1.42 billion, a hair under the $1.43 billion expected. EPS was $0.51 against $0.55 forecast. Crypto revenue rose to $120 million from $100 million in Q2, up 20% sequentially, though still 55% below last year’s $268 million. Event contracts are now the bigger business: $173 million, up from $156 million, on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, more than seven times a year ago. Between prediction markets and crypto, more than a fifth of Robinhood’s revenue now comes from products that barely existed two years ago.
And then came the call and Vlad’s commentary on Robinhood Chain.
Vlad admitted that Robinhood Chain has outrun their internal forecasts and expectations. The chain launched July 1. By late August it was generating more fees over a rolling 30 days than Ethereum or Base. Tenev said they’ve had to staff up a team to keep pace, and that builders have been telling them Robinhood could be doing more.
His response: “You should expect to see us really ramping the investment, because you just don’t see growth of a new ecosystem like this. It’s an uncommon thing. A lot of chains have launched over the past few months that have had an incomparably small level of traction compared to this. So we’re doubling down.”
Then he described where he thinks it goes: “Imagine if you take a stock token, make it fully programmable just like software. What can you do? Can you have tokenized options contracts?”
This was music to the Robinhood Chain bulls’ ears. And it was enough to send the Robinhood Chain leaders up 20-50% across the board, led by Pons +18%, AI (Long) +33% and Orbio +57%.

Neither was Robinhood’s idea, and both only exist because the stock tokens do.
Now those teams can expect more support from the Robinhood team. Two tweets from Robinhood Crypto on Tuesday already evidence this leaning in, supporting both Long and Priors. So earnings may have been a miss, but the earnings call was a big win. Now let’s see just what leaning in means…

title: Moody's Rates Ripple's $2.6B RLUSD Stablecoin A2, a Day After OCC Bank Approval - Decrypt
text:
Moody's Ratings has assigned an A2 long-term deposit rating and a P-1 short-term deposit rating to Ripple USD (RLUSD), the dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Ripple subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company, the agency said on Tuesday.
A2 is the sixth-highest long-term grade on Moody's scale, and P-1 is its top short-term grade. The agency said the ratings reflect the quality of RLUSD's reserves, which are held mainly in Treasury bills, other short-term U.S. government assets and cash, most of it with custodian BNY. Eligible institutional holders can redeem RLUSD at par within two business days.
Moody's also flagged gaps in holders' protection, noting that Standard Custody is not a bankruptcy-remote entity, and RLUSD holders do not currently have a direct ownership interest in the reserves—though the agency said the GENIUS Act, the U.S. stablecoin law due to take effect in 2027, will exclude required reserves from an issuer's bankruptcy estate. The ratings were requested by the issuer, Moody's said.
The rating came a day after Ripple won final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for Ripple National Trust Bank, which will manage RLUSD's reserves and act as their collateral trustee. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody under New York Department of Financial Services oversight, putting the stablecoin under both state and federal supervision.
Launched in December 2024 on Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, RLUSD has a market capitalization of about $2.6 billion, according to CoinGecko, still a small share of a stablecoin market worth some $300 billion.
Ripple has pitched the token at institutions rather than retail traders. Earlier this month, Standard Chartered began offering institutional custody of RLUSD through its Dubai branch, and said it was working with Ripple and LMAX Group on a "collateral mirroring" setup that would let clients use the stablecoin as trading collateral without moving it off the bank's books.
In November 2025, Ripple teamed up with Mastercard, WebBank and Gemini to explore using RLUSD on the XRP Ledger to settle fiat transactions on the Gemini Credit Card, pending regulatory approvals. RLUSD had just passed a $1 billion market cap at the time, making it the 11th-largest stablecoin, according to DefiLlama.

The venue would operate under the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” which allows qualifying platforms to trade tokenized stocks using automated market makers. Companies have 30 days after notification to object to their inclusion.
OKXICE co-chairman Andrew Cuomo previously said many companies were expected to wait and see how the market develops before participating, describing the SEC’s limited experiment as “a sandbox—a model demonstration.”

title: Ripple expects $900 million annualized product revenue run rate as institutional business expands
text: Ripple expects to exit 2026 with a $900 million annualized product revenue run rate, citing growth across its payments, custody, stablecoin, prime brokerage, and treasury businesses, the firm announced Wednesday. The digital asset infrastructure firm said customers and partners using multiple Ripple products have tripled this year, as its payments network is expected to approach $150 billion in lifetime volume by year-end and its RLUSD stablecoin reaches a $2.6 billion market capitalization. "As traditional and digital finance converge, market infrastructure is migrating to modern rails," Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in a statement. "Settlement is moving to real-time, 24/7, and tokenized assets can be traded, financed and used as collateral." On Monday, Ripple also received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, while expanding its partnership with BNY on tokenized trade finance using the XRP Ledger. That push is extending beyond payments and stablecoins, as financial institutions increasingly use Ripple's infrastructure for tokenized assets and trading. Ripple's big year Aviva Investors just launched a tokenized share class of its £22 billion sterling liquidity fund on XRPL, investing £50 million ($66.7 million) in the new share class. The hedge fund Brevan Howard expanded its relationship with Ripple to include prime brokerage, clearing and financing. Meanwhile, Ripple Prime earlier this month added swaps referencing more than 100 markets, with 24/7 trading and settlement. Institutional clients can use RLUSD as collateral. On a more cultural note, Ripple also became the Kansas Jayhawks' sports sponsor — the first time a cryptocurrency would be displayed on the jerseys of a major college sports program. That was followed by similar deals with Florida Gators athletics and the University of Louisville. "Others focus on individual pieces of the puzzle," Garlinghouse said Wednesday. "Ripple is bringing all of that together, with our partners, to enable the Internet of Value." Despite a spike higher in early August, the XRP token remains down nearly 30% this year with an $83 billion market cap. Meanwhile, spot XRP ETF volumes have increased in recent months, although they still pale in comparison to their BTC, ETH, and SOL ETF counterparts. A New York startup founded by Wall Street alumni wants to put American apartment, farm, and energy loans on public blockchains, and it just raised the money to start.
Birch Hill said Wednesday it closed a $4 million seed round led by Multicoin Capital, with participation from ParaFi Capital, Castle Island Ventures, and Nascent. The round brings its total funding to $6.5 million.
The firm is led by CEO Bhavin Vaid, a former Goldman Sachs investment banking analyst who later worked in private equity at Cerberus Capital Management and co-founded crypto investment firm Halo Capital. Co-founder and COO Connor Flanagan spent more than four years at BlackRock, including on its Aladdin risk platform, before roles at Digital Currency Group and analytics firm Flipside.
Birch Hill operates in three divisions. Its Vaults arm is an official curator on Morpho, an onchain lending protocol, where it assesses credit and sets risk parameters for vaults and markets. Its Strategies unit builds onchain credit products, including a strategy called Birch Hill Absolute Value. Its Enterprise division has applied to FINRA for broker-dealer membership, which would let it place private credit offerings with verified accredited investors.
“Loan originators need new sources of capital, and onchain lenders need credit they can trust,” Vaid said in a statement.
Longer term, the firm plans to securitize pools of U.S. multifamily, agriculture, and energy loans designed to be held onchain within the U.S. regulatory framework. Birch Hill said it met with the SEC’s Crypto Task Force in August as part of that effort. It argues that banks, insurers, and other fiduciaries will only allocate to credit packaged in structures they recognize.
The round funds an eight-person team that includes three hires from vault platform Yearn: Brad Schlagel, who led development of Yearn v3, Ian Plosker, and Alex Cornwell. Traver Normandi joins from risk management firm Gauntlet to lead business development.
“Private credit is a fragmented, relationship-driven market, which makes it one of the clearest opportunities to build new financial infrastructure onchain,” said Shayon Sengupta, general partner and co-head of venture at Multicoin.
The raise comes as Washington warms to onchain finance. The SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets in August, which would let projects raise money through token sales without full registration. title: Wall Street giant DTCC launches tokenization for stocks, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries
text:
The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the giant at the heart of U.S. securities markets, went live with its tokenization service Wednesday, taking a step toward bringing stocks, bonds and funds onto blockchain infrastructure.
The service is available on the Canton Network CC$0.1146 and DTCC's private Besu blockchain, initially supporting select large-cap stocks from the Russell 1000 index, exchange-traded funds (ETF) and U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds. DTCC’s product website says 34 securities are eligible at launch, which represent approximately $30 trillion market value, a DTCC spokesperson told CoinDesk.
The debut is a significant step for Wall Street's tokenization push because DTCC sits at the center of how U.S. securities markets work. Through its subsidiaries, the firm handles clearing, settlement and custody for much of the country's stock and bond trading, with more than $114 trillion in securities held at its depository.
The company’s road map includes adding Stellar XLM$0.1701 and stablecoin issuer Circle Internet's Arc blockchain next year, along with broader corporate-action support and tools for settling transactions with digital cash.
The tokens are backed one-for-one by securities held at DTCC subsidiary Depository Trust Company (DTC), and can move between registered wallets around the clock.
Bringing blockchain technology into the system could make tokenized assets part of mainstream market infrastructure rather than a separate market operating alongside it.
Tokenization promises to make financial assets easier to transfer, settle and use as collateral. While banks and asset managers have spent years experimenting with blockchain-based securities, connecting those assets to the systems that already underpin trillions of dollars in transactions could help bring the technology into everyday market operations.
Analysts at Citi projected tokenized securities will become a $5.5 trillion market by 2030 as more financial institutions adopt blockchain technology.
"Today marks the culmination of years of work to bring tokenized securities into a regulated framework supported by trusted market infrastructure," said Frank La Salla, DTCC's president and CEO.
"By extending DTC's resiliency, governance and operational standards into digital markets, we are establishing the foundation for responsible institutional adoption at scale."
Twenty participants have signed agreements to access the service, including Bank of America, Barclays, Citi, Fidelity Investments, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Citadel Securities, State Street and UBS. DTCC said more firms will join over time.
Eligible firms can convert securities into tokens during business hours, with DTCC targeting processing times of 15 minutes or less. Once tokenized, the assets can move between registered blockchain wallets around the clock, subject to compliance restrictions.
The service keeps official ownership records with DTC even as tokens move between registered wallets. That structure sets the approach apart from synthetic stock tokens that track share prices without granting ownership of the underlying securities. DTCC's tokens represent securities already held in custody, preserving their existing rights.
The rollout follows a demonstration earlier this year and plans announced in May.
In addition to adding Stellar and Arc in 2027, DTCC plans to add tools for settling transactions with digital cash and using tokenized securities as collateral.
The service builds on a December no-action letter by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which allowed DTCC to tokenize a defined set of securities.
Other market operators are moving in the same direction. Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) are developing tokenized securities trading infrastructure, while NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) is set to operate a blockchain-based trading venue under the SEC’s innovation exemption with crypto exchange OKX.

title: Cybersecurity ‘Armageddon’: How to Stay Safe Online
text:
Each day brings news of another AI-powered attack, or a newly discovered vulnerability. Here’s what’s happening and how ordinary people can protect themselves online.
Cybersecurity professionals are having a brutal month.
What’s being dubbed Black October isn’t even over, and it’s already brought about several dozen major cyberattacks and AI-identified vulnerabilities across the internet.
When critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by around 70% of websites, were uncovered with the help of AI tools and disclosed by the PHP Foundation on Oct. 21, the race to patch servers around the world began.
Cloud services provider Cloudflare reported millions of attempts to exploit the vulnerability after its disclosure, following thousands of attempts in the preceding hours.
Some countries, including France and Finland, temporarily pulled access to certain websites while the US National Security Agency (NSA) warned organizations to patch the flaws immediately or take affected systems offline.
“We are at Security Armageddon now,” said NEAR founder Illia Polosukhin. Anthropic’s chief security adviser Jason Clinton warned that, “as bad as things have gotten in the past 4 days, they are going to get a lot worse before they get better.”
Citizens of the United Kingdom are even being urged to “be ready” for an emergency, such as severe weather or cyberattacks, that could cut off access to critical infrastructure such as water, electricity or the internet. US military installation have been told to prep for 90 days of independent operation under the FORTRESS initiative.
Beyond rushing out to stockpile canned food and walkie-talkies, is there anything else ordinary people can do to mitigate their exposure?
“It’s really bad. It looks like the rest of the internet is waking up to the reality we had three months ago,” Rob Hamilton, a Bitcoin security researcher involved in the Bitcoin Red Team, tells Magazine.
UK government is urging citizens to be ready for an emergency. Source: gov.uk
In the past week or so, cloud platform Railway disclosed that an attacker has accessed and decrypted customer credentials and API keys, apparently targeting AI providers.
Related: France is world’s most dangerous place for Bitcoiners: 90 attacks in 7 months
Medical testing giant Quest Diagnostics confirmed a breach of private patient health data, while Indian security firm eMudhra was found to have eight digital certificate authorities with weak keys that could potentially have let attackers impersonate trusted websites. And code hosting platform GitHub experienced a major service disruption that highlighted how heavily the software world relies on shared infrastructure.
GitHub’s senior director of security, Austin Devers, says incidents like this are a “clear reminder that reliability requires constant work,” because modern development is “so connected.”
Railway security incident. Source: Railway
Jonathan Riss, an OSINT and blockchain intelligence analyst at blockchain security firm CertiK, tells Magazine:
Unfortunately, he adds that AI’s ability to find vulnerabilities is not matched by its ability to fix them:
One reason the problem is getting worse is because AI has changed the economics of cybersecurity.
What once required nation-state resources and sophisticated hackers to pull off can now be achieved by a teenager in a basement somewhere.
AI entrepreneur and investor Matt Shumer said that AI enables non technical users to find weak spots and exploit them, leaving defenders are “racing to keep up.”
Devers says AI-assisted security tools are “dramatically” lowering the barrier to “uncovering complex, deep-seated flaws in widely used codebases.”
Related: Keystone says website breach exposed hardware wallet buyers’ addresses
There are some practical steps ordinary folk can use to stay safer online during this volatile period.
The internet is under attack. Source: Matt Shumer
Shumer recommends staying off sites you don’t know, and definitely don’t enter passwords or card numbers into unfamiliar sites “until this blows over” since smaller sites are the “least likely to have patched.”
Delete any apps you don’t use and unplug smart gadgets you don’t need. Keep some cash at home and enough groceries for a few days, “if you want to be extra careful.”
Devers says the best defense is “locking down personal access points and keeping overall footprints small.” Turn on Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all accounts, ideally using an authenticator app or hardware security key rather than text messages.
Never reuse passwords either, he says. “Create strong, unique passwords for every site, and periodically disconnect old app permissions or third-party connections you no longer use.” Keep your devices and web browsers updated automatically:
While the alarming rise in security incidents has caused some crypto holders to consider alternatives and some experts to advise against self-custody, others, such as Bitcoin advocate and Casa chief security officer Jameson Lopp, remind users that defeats the whole purpose.
Riss recommends separating small amounts you intend to use into a hot wallet, from longer-term holdings in a hardware wallet, and to “actually read what you’re signing rather than approving blind.”
While these precautions can reduce your vulnerability to attack, everyday users can only lock down local issues, and have little ability to affect wider problems.
You can “reduce blast radius,” he says, “not prevent infrastructure compromise.”
So while users can improve their cyber hygiene, ultimately, “the structural burden sits with platforms and providers.”

title: House Oversight Chair Comer Probes Delaware Plan for AI-Run Companies - Decrypt
text:
House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer (R-KY) is investigating Delaware's effort to create a new kind of corporate entity run by an artificial intelligence agent, the committee said on Monday.
In a letter to Delaware Gov. Matt Meyer, Comer raised concerns about the proposed Artificial Intelligence Company, or AIC, which would give the person or entity behind it protection from liability for harms caused by the AI agent running it.
🚨 Delaware wants to let AI agents run companies while shielding their owners from liability when the AI causes harm.
Chairman @RepJamesComer is seeking documents, including internal AI chat logs, from Gov. Meyer to find out who’s behind the plan. https://t.co/tPzK0qFC4C
— Oversight Committee (@GOPoversight) October 26, 2026
"We are concerned that Delaware's AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives," Comer wrote.
The letter questions the role of private-sector contributors to the proposal. It notes that a December 2025 report by Delaware's AI Commission made no mention of efforts to assess safety risks or consult independent experts, and that the Secretary of State's office declined to tell reporters about its working relationship with an AI company involved in the project.
Comer asked Meyer to hand over all documents and communications about the AIC's development since January 2025, including "internal AI chat logs," along with agreements with outside contributors, records on safety concerns and all drafts of the proposal, by November 9. The committee said the information could inform federal legislation, including proposals to limit state AI regulatory initiatives.
Delaware Secretary of State Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez and John Nay, CEO of legal AI firm Norm Ai, unveiled the proposal in a Fortune op-ed in July, describing a public-private partnership led by Norm Ai.
An AIC would be able to sue and be sued, hold property and take on obligations at its AI agent's direction. It would have a single member responsible for keeping it adequately capitalized, and that member would be shielded from its debts unless it failed to capitalize the company or used it to commit fraud or a willful violation of law. AICs would operate only within a 30-month regulatory sandbox overseen by a committee of state officials and outside experts, would have to disclose their status to counterparties, and would be barred from banking.
The proposal aims to "wrap AI in legal form," the authors wrote, arguing that a recognizable legal identity would make an autonomous system's conduct "visible, traceable, and accountable."
Some legal scholars have questioned that reasoning. "There's really no overarching regulatory plan here for dealing with the fallout that AI-governed companies could bring," Christopher Bruner, a business law professor at the University of Georgia, told WHYY in September.
Patibanda-Sanchez has rejected the idea that the plan is a liability shield. "We're not trying to shield liability. We're trying to define where exactly liability lands when there's some type of malfeasance or psychopathic behavior," she told Bloomberg Law in July.
Meyer has also defended the effort. "It is coming, and the solution is not ignoring it," he said on a WHYY call-in show in September. State lawmakers are expected to consider draft legislation when they return in January.
